tagline: Out on the ridges over what Lewis and Clark called desert.
intro: From Winifred the byway takes gravel and unimproved back roads north and east onto the ridges above the Missouri, through the Upper Missouri River Breaks National Monument, and comes out at US 191 near the Fred Robinson Bridge. Below it runs the Upper Missouri National Wild and Scenic River, where the land breaks away to the water in steep bluffs and rock outcrops.

Lewis and Clark came through in 1805 and called this country the Deserts of America. The fur traders who followed named this stretch of river Mauvaises Terres, the bad lands. Much of it still looks the way the expedition found it.

moments.title: Winifred
moments.text: The town began in 1913 at the end of a Milwaukee Road branch line and is popularly said to be named for a railroad owner's daughter, the other daughter getting Christina, 15 miles off.

moments.title: Deweese Ridge
moments.text: From Winifred to here the road keeps close to the trail of the Nez Perce, who crossed the Missouri into the Breaks in 1877 trying to reach Canada.

moments.title: Fred Robinson Bridge
moments.text: Near the end of the byway a four-span steel-girder bridge crosses the Missouri, named for a state senator who was among its most aggressive backers.

practical: The byway is gravel and unimproved road that becomes totally impassable when wet, so do not set out if wet weather threatens.
